is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles arabiensis (Abstract, page 1).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study only performs species identification PCR (Scott et al. 1993) and does not genotype any insecticide-resistance markers such as Vgsc (kdr), Ace-1, or GSTe2 (Methods, page 3; Results, page 3).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: No genotype data for resistance markers is reported. Only bioassay mortality and knockdown times are provided (Tables 1-6).

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected as larvae from rice fields in Mabogini village, Tanzania (Methods, page 2).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary empirical study investigating the influence of age and season on insecticide susceptibility.

sub_country_location.evidence: Data is tied to Mabogini village, Lower Moshi rice irrigation scheme (Methods, page 2).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Collections were conducted in 2013 and 2014 (Methods, page 2).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study describes original field collections in Mabogini, Tanzania, in 2013-2014.

supplement.evidence: The paper does not mention any supplementary files containing genotype data.

assessment.summary: The study investigated the effect of age and seasonality on insecticide resistance in Anopheles arabiensis from northern Tanzania. While it reports extensive bioassay data for multiple insecticides (deltamethrin, permethrin, lambda-cyhalothrin, DDT, bendiocarb, and pirimiphos-methyl) across different age groups and seasons, it does not report any genotyping of insecticide-resistance markers. PCR was only used for species identification.
exclusion_reasons: The study does not report genotyping of any of the target insecticide-resistance markers (e.g., Vgsc, Ace-1, Rdl, GSTe2). It only reports species identification and bioassay results.
